fields.v: Yan, C., Xu, Z., Li, Y., Xu, S., Liu, Y., Deng, G., Ma, S. (2026). One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.11647v2 [cs.SE], 13 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.11647v2 [cs.SE], 13 Oct 2026; ACM journal-style template, no venue stated
University of New South Wales (Yan, Xu Z., Li, Xu S.); Griffith University (Liu); Nanyang Technological University (Deng); The University of Wollongong (Ma)

Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — empirical study: repository mining of 20,947 repositories for co-installed similar skills plus a controlled experiment (6,368 Claude Code runs on 312 skill pairs); proposes a requirement-level core-function fidelity measure; also tests the authors' own pre-tool hook guard as a mitigation
fields.why: Main nature Evaluates (repository mining plus controlled experiment) is clear. The secondary is open: the fidelity measure is presented as a contribution (Proposes an evaluation method), but the guard hook is also a contribution tested in its own randomized experiment (pp. 4, 12, 16), which would make the secondary 'Proposes an approach'; that choice also decides Q12 and Q13
fields.doubt: A natureza principal (Evaluates) é clara. Decide a secundária: a medida de fidelidade (Proposes an evaluation method) ou o hook de guarda, testado em experiência própria (Proposes an approach); isto afeta Q12 e Q13.

fields.v: Agent Skills (SKILL.md directories, Anthropic open standard) in Claude Code 2.1.283; installed skill A vs similar skill B vs unrelated skill C at project, personal and plugin scopes; guard = pre-tool hook denying first read of B (authors' own). Cross-check on Codex

SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, when_to_use) and Markdown body of instructions, optional scripts; listing of names and descriptions in context (description truncated at 1,536 characters; listing capped at 1% of context, raised to 20,000 characters in the study). Study artefacts: core functions (quoted, unique, checkable requirements) and checks per case

Skill flow: listing of skill names/descriptions placed in context -> model selects and invokes a skill (or reads its files) -> body loaded and followed. Study flow: installation reconstruction -> pair mining (embedding retrieval, LLM pair judge) -> case building (core functions, request, repository, checks) -> controlled runs (Fig. 2)
None in the skill flow (the model chooses out of sight; disclosure to the user measured). Study: two human raters validate every LLM-assisted step on random samples
Single artefact (skill files) in full agent runs
Not classifiable (agent skills / instruction files; no specification; authors do not use SDD terms)
Existing code base (small, LLM-drafted synthetic starting repository of at most 15 files, one per case) with an LLM-drafted request for the job of the installed skill; skills mined from real projects
fields.why: Each run starts from an LLM-drafted repository of at most 15 files (p. 9), so 'existing code base' fits formally, but the repositories are tiny and synthetic and many requests are documentation or process tasks
fields.doubt: Cada execução parte de um repositório sintético com até 15 ficheiros (p. 9). Decide se conta como 'existing code base' ou se a distinção não se aplica a estas tarefas.

General software development skills (normative, capability and script-bearing; e.g., pull-request formats, release checklists, safety rules, document handling); programming languages Not stated
N/A (no participants; two human raters are authors)

Not used as outcome. Reported descriptively per configuration (Table 3): tool calls and hours of agent time, e.g. only A 24,617 calls / 81.3 h, only B 24,400 / 78.7 h, A+B 24,555 / 81.6 h, swapped 24,633 / 81.9 h, personal 6,891 / 22.3 h, plugin 6,749 / 22.8 h, A+C 25,234 / 68.8 h, guard experiment 18,192 / 54.0 h. Study totals: 6.3 billion input and 110 million output tokens, about $5,550 at API prices, 542.4 h agent time, 169,294 tool calls

Fidelity: share of the first three applicable core functions of the installed skill fulfilled (also on exclusive vs shared core functions); skill use (invocation or file reads); substitution vs interference; disclosure in the final reply; prevalence of conflicting pairs

Automatic: scripts decide 327 of 921 primary core functions; output judge GPT-6 Astra (blinded to configuration and to which skill is A) decides the other 594, undecidable script checks and all but 11 task-completion checks; tool-call logs for skill use. Human validation of every LLM-assisted step on random samples: Krippendorff's alpha 0.74-0.88 between the two raters and 0.71-0.84 between their consensus and the LLM (output judge: 0.78 core functions, 0.75 task completion, 0.84 disclosure). Paired risk differences with 95% CIs over pairs, Holm correction

Agent Claude Code 2.1.283; models Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 (20251001), Opus 5; pooled values (per-model values mostly in Fig. 4-6 only); one run per pair x configuration x model. Metrics: fidelity, task completion, use of A. No success criterion stated by the authors for any configuration, so no verdicts; cost per configuration only as agent hours and tool calls (Table 3).
- Only A (baseline): fidelity 57.3%, task completion 57.2%; 30.3% of runs do not use A; 81.3 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Only B: fidelity 46.3%, completion 58.1%; 78.7 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- A+B: use of A -19.9 pp, completion +1.9 pp (n.s.), fidelity -2.6 pp, exclusive core functions -5.6 pp vs only A; 12.1% of runs use only B, 38.0% neither; 81.6 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- A+C (unrelated skill): use of A -5.9 pp, fidelity -0.2 pp; 68.8 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Swapped order: listing order changes use of A by +0.6 pp (renaming +4.4 pp); 81.9 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- B personal scope (81 same-name pairs): use of A -35.0 pp, fidelity -3.9 pp; 22.3 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- B plugin scope (81 pairs): B used in 2.9%, use of A -6.2 pp; 22.8 h. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- A+B with guard hook (187 pair-model combinations, vs without): switch to A after 96% of denials; exclusive fidelity +9.1 pp overall, +17.8 pp where both runs reached for B first; completion +4.1 pp (n.s.); 54.0 h for both arms. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Per model in A+B: Opus 5 uses both skills in 36.8% of runs, neither in 15.5%; Haiku 4.5 neither in 56.4%
- Codex check (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, 193 pairs): use of A -18.2 pp, exclusive fidelity -3.4 pp, task completion not lowered. No criterion stated by the authors

Tasks: 312 cases (request + starting repository + checks), one per pair. Configurations: only A, only B, A+B, swapped, personal scope, plugin scope, A+C, A+B with/without guard; three models. Baseline: only A. Held constant: request, repository, container image, Claude Code version, 80 turns / 25 min limit, listing cap; one factor changed at a time. Acceptance: core functions and checks fixed before any run; scripts + blinded LLM judge. Repetitions: one run per pair x configuration x model; 512 combinations repeated 2-3 times (ICC 0.78 / 0.84). Human intervention: none (non-interactive)

Co-installing a similar skill lowers use of A by 19.9 pp [-23.1, -16.7] and fidelity by 2.6 pp [-4.4, -0.8] (exclusive 5.6 pp [-7.3, -3.8]) without lowering task completion (+1.9 [-1.0, +4.9]); unrelated skill only -5.9 pp use. Substituted runs carry 36% of fidelity loss, neither-skill runs 45%. Scope decides: personal same-name skill overrides A (-35.0 pp). Substitution disclosed in 0.9% of runs. Opening B first: -9.4 pp exclusive fidelity (Holm p=0.004). Guard recovers the 16.5 pp loss; significant for every model

Yes: fidelity separated configurations where task completion did not (only A vs only B: 11.0 pp fidelity gap at equal completion). Repeatable: repeated runs agree (88.9%, ICC 0.78-0.84); effects replicated on Codex. Limitations stated: single runs per combination; first read observed rather than assigned (guard randomized); cross-project pairs constructed; full design on Claude Code only

Nondeterministic single runs; full design only on Claude Code (Codex check on 193 pairs); cross-project pairs constructed; prevalence conservative (personal skills and plugins not visible in public repos). Implications: benchmarks should score exclusive core functions; platforms should guard the first read, show which skill ran, let projects declare which skill wins; authors should use distinctive names and descriptions

Fig. 4-6 hold most per-model and per-type values (values in figures only). LLM-heavy pipeline: GPT-6 Astra for repository typing, pair judging, skill typing, core-function extraction, case drafting and output judging; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B for retrieval. Replication package at https://github.com/ltroin/conflict (harness, cases, all 6,368 run logs, scripts). Core functions fixed before runs, no formal pre-registration. pdftotext file contains non-UTF-8 symbols for the A/B/C markers. Programming language: Not stated

Partly (0.5): checks fixed before runs and decided by scripts (327 of 921 core functions) or a blinded LLM judge validated by two human raters (consensus-LLM alpha 0.78 on core functions, 0.75 on task completion); most core functions judged by LLM rather than tests
fields.why: Checks fixed before runs; scripts decide 327 of 921 primary core functions and a blinded LLM judge the rest and almost all task completion, validated by two human raters (consensus-LLM alpha 0.78 core functions, 0.75 task completion, p. 12). Whether a validated blinded LLM judge counts as an independent criterion (Yes) or Partly is a judgement
fields.doubt: A maioria das verificações é decidida por um juiz LLM cego, validado por dois avaliadores humanos (alfa 0,75-0,78). Decide se isso conta como critério independente (Yes) ou só Partly.
